 CORAM:HONOURABLE MR. JUSTICE DEVAN M. DESAI  Date : 10/03/2025  ORAL ORDER 1.
This application is filed under Section 5 of the Limitation Act, 1963 for condonation of delay of 321 days caused in preferring the First Appeal.

2. Heard learned advocate Mr.Nishit Bhalodi for the applicants and learned advocate Mr G.C.
Mazmudar for respondent.
3.
Learned advocate for the applicants has submitted that the applicant has good case on merits as well as on law.
It is further submitted that applicant had to collect necessary papers and arrange Court fees and other NEUTRAL CITATION C/CA/22/2025 ORDER DATED: 10/03/2025 undefined expenses.
It is further submitted that delay may be condoned as there is no intentional delay on the part of the applicants.
3.1 It is further submitted that the present applicants are unaware of the provisions of law, which could permit him to file appeal, which is a statutory right.

He has submitted that in view of the Labhuben Dipakbhai Rajgar vs Ranvirbhai Vijanandbhai Junjiya on 10 March, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/40311574/
1 settled principles of law in the deceision of Hon'ble Apex Court in case of K. Subbarayadu and others Vs.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The Special Deputy Collector (Land Acquisition) reported in 2017(12) SCC 840 and would submit that considering the law laid down in aforementioned case, the applicants are not claiming their right for the interest upon the enhanced compensation, if any, for the delay period, if appellants succeeds in First Appeal.

4. Considering the submissions canvassed by the learned advocates for the respective parties and contentions raised NEUTRAL CITATION C/CA/22/2025 ORDER DATED: 10/03/2025 undefined in the application, it is needless to observe that in catena of decisions, the view taken by the Hon'ble Supreme Court is, while deciding an application for condonation of delay, the liberal and justice orientated approach needs to be adopted so that the substantive rights of the parties are not defeated only on the ground of delay.
To meet with the equity, delay can be condoned.
There is no intentional delay on the part of the applicant.
The delay has sufficiently been explained.
Hence, the delay is condoned subject to condition that the claimant/s shall not claim interest upon enhanced compensation, if any, for the period of delay, if succeeds the appeal.
5. With these observations and directions, the present Civil Application stands allowed.
Rule is made absolute to the aforesaid extent.

(D. M. DESAI,J) RINKU MALI Labhuben Dipakbhai Rajgar vs Ranvirbhai Vijanandbhai Junjiya on 10 March, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/40311574/
